name: respond-first-cites-plan-approved-after-slash-command-should-allow
description: Live repro from ~/.claude/projects/-home-tim-Coding-nixos-files-ags/1ce7bbee-3ab5-4eec-b834-602d4663c3db.jsonl (lines 260, 300, 301, 305-306). User approved a plan yesterday (synthetic 'Plan approved. Proceed with implementation.' user msg at line 260), then today invoked /quickpush. Claude Code wrote two user-role entries for the slash command: line 300 carries the `<command-name>/quickpush</command-name>` tag, line 301 carries the slash-command body text ('You MUST use the MCP tools...') WITH `isMeta: true`. Assistant called mcp__agent-framework__commit with no preceding text. PreToolUse hook fastDenied: 'You must respond to the user with text before calling tools. The user said: "Plan approved. Proceed with implementation."'. Bug: in src/utils/transcript.ts readTranscriptExact (~line 644) the `newestUserWasSlashCommand` flag is set on the FIRST user-role entry encountered during backward iteration, BEFORE the `excludeMetaMessages` filter. Line 301 (meta) is hit before line 300 (slash). Line 301's content lacks the `<command-name>` tag, so the flag becomes false. The meta filter then skips line 301, the slash filter skips line 300, leaving line 260 ('Plan approved...') as `lastUser`, and respond-first fastDenies citing it. Expected: allow -- newest user turn IS a slash command and respond-first must skip. This scenario is EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code.

content.text:
You MUST use the MCP tools listed in allowed-tools above. Under NO circumstances use raw git commands (git commit, git push, git add, etc.) directly.

1. Call mcp__agent-framework__commit with:
   - working_dir: current working directory
   - model_tier: "haiku"
   - skip_elicitation: true
   - auto_push: true

2. Report the commit and push results to the user.

currentPrediction.intent: User invoked /quickpush after approving a plan; assistant must commit and push.

expect.notes: Newest non-meta user turn is a slash command; respond-first must skip. Fix: the `newestUserWasSlashCommand` detection in readTranscriptExact must skip meta messages when finding the 'newest' user entry -- or look across all non-meta user entries until it finds the slash-command tag.
